svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Radiation from the Sun is mostly short-wavelength. It passes through the atmosphere."], [2, "About 30% is reflected straight back to space by clouds, ice and the surface."], [3.5, "The surface absorbs the rest and warms up. It emits long-wavelength infrared radiation."], [6, "Greenhouse gases absorb some of the infrared, then re-emit it in all directions, some back to the surface."], [9, "The rest escapes to space. This natural greenhouse effect keeps Earth about 33 \u00b0C warmer than it would be."], [11.5, "Adding CO\u2082 and methane traps more infrared: the enhanced greenhouse effect causes global warming."]]
svg.title: The greenhouse effect
svg.desc: Short-wavelength radiation from the Sun passes through the atmosphere; some is reflected; the surface emits infrared, which greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit, some back to the surface.
svg.text: Yellow: short-wavelength solar radiation. Red: long-wavelength infrared. Not to scale.

g.data-info: Emits mainly short-wavelength radiation (visible and near-infrared, some ultraviolet).
Carbon dioxide, methane, water vapour and nitrous oxide are transparent to most short-wavelength radiation but absorb long-wavelength infrared.
g.text: CO₂, CH₄, H₂O greenhouse gas molecules

g.data-info: Absorbs short-wavelength radiation and warms up; it emits long-wavelength infrared radiation.
About 30% is reflected by clouds, ice and the surface (albedo) without warming.
Greenhouse gas molecules absorb infrared and re-emit it in all directions, some back towards the surface, which keeps it warmer.

g.text: greenhouse gases absorb infrared and re-emit it, some back to the surface

g.data-info: Some infrared escapes. More greenhouse gas means less escapes: the enhanced greenhouse effect and global warming.

g.text: more CO₂ and CH₄ → more infrared trapped → enhanced greenhouse effect
